operational_simulation.organization_and_actor: Brazilian residential developer or construction company with a post-handover service team; warranty coordinator, technical-assistance engineer, and customer-service analyst
processes: receive and normalize homeowner warranty or defect requests from portal, email, messaging, photos, and voice-note transcription
classify the building system, location, urgency, likely warranty path, and required evidence before technical inspection
route recurring defect descriptions to the responsible contractor and preserve a reviewable service history
operational_simulation.deterministic_baseline: official intake channel, mandatory structured fields, unit and room identifiers, warranty matrix, owner manual, rule-based eligibility, attachment checklist, queue routing, SLA, and engineer review
operational_simulation.remaining_gap: Compact Portuguese NLP could reduce manual normalization and routing of free-text requests, but the bounded value is already covered by structured post-handover workflows and current warranty-management products that centralize, categorize, assign, and track claims.

training_data.observation_unit: one post-handover service request at the first complete triage point
training_data.input_data: request text or transcription plus unit, room, system, delivery date, warranty item, declared urgency, and attachment-presence fields available before routing
training_data.target_or_reward: engineer-confirmed defect category, responsible queue or contractor, evidence-completeness class, and valid escalation outcome
training_data.label_source: historical ticket resolution, engineer correction, contractor reassignment, inspection result, and explicit false-routing review
training_data.prediction_time: after minimum intake validation and before technical assignment or site inspection
training_data.expected_volume: unknown; must be measured per developer, portfolio size, delivery cohort, channel, and warranty period
training_data.class_balance: rare safety-critical or structural cases are likely minority classes; exact distribution is unknown
training_data.historical_coverage: requires multiple developments, building systems, suppliers, delivery periods, customer vocabularies, and both accepted and rejected warranty requests
training_data.train_validation_split: hold out later delivery cohorts and entire developments; prevent repeated messages, follow-ups, and the same defect case from crossing splits
training_data.leakage_risks: using inspection findings, final responsibility, contractor response, warranty approval, repair outcome, or fields added after initial routing
training_data.representativeness_risks: different construction methods, manuals, regional vocabulary, resident communication quality, channels, suppliers, and company-specific category taxonomies
training_data.feedback_loop: engineer recategorization, queue reassignment, inspection result, request closure reason, and explicit false-positive or abstention correction
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: protect resident identity, contact data, unit location, images of private homes, accessibility information, and evidence shared with contractors
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: retain structured intake, deterministic warranty rules, keyword search, mandatory evidence checks, manual triage, and existing post-handover service platforms

portfolio_coherence.reason: The remaining NLP task is bounded classification and routing inside a post-handover workflow. Current Brazilian and international products already centralize warranty requests, capture evidence, categorize defects, assign ownership, and track resolution; a smaller classifier is an implementation option, not a differentiated opportunity.
